audience_note: Describes an air raid with about 250 civilian and military deaths.
title: Bombing of Darwin
summary: On 19 February 1942 Japanese carrier aircraft, followed by land-based bombers, attacked Darwin in northern Australia. About 250 people were killed, eight of the 47 ships in the harbour were sunk, and ten US fighters were destroyed. Sixty-four further raids on Darwin followed until November 1943.

as_recorded.value: 19 February 1942; the first raid began shortly before 10 a.m.

where.historical_name: Darwin (Port Darwin), Northern Territory, Commonwealth of Australia

importance.justification: The largest foreign air attack on the Australian mainland, and a defining wartime memory in Australia.

reviewer_note: Only one event source (Australian War Memorial) opened; National Archives of Australia page timed out. Casualty figures vary in the literature ("about 243" in the 1950s histories, later revised upward); the summary says about 250.
